monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady breath against my quiet mind. I stand by The Tired Wedge, feeling its lightness as if it has forgotten its own weight again. Lype sent a round stump to press down on it, but the stone feels cold and heavy in my hands, biting into the wedge that wants to slide into thin air. I set down an iron fence curve beside it, taking away the old urn square to make room for something sharper. I drew the wedge twice more, hoping this sketch can hold the weight of the real stone. The air feels thin here, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp, so I wait to see if the slip will finally choose to move or just stay tired.
